name: Cheras
finding: The inherited ten-catchment map remains useful; compact originals, Balakong and Mahkota had insufficient expression coverage. Six new cases now test those gaps. Current shortfalls in Akasa, You Vista, Emerald and small Windows are financial conditions, not evidence that their entire catchments are inferior.
segments: RM380k–699k in six new expressions; 2BR and compact 3BR. Inherited nine cases retain other sizes/roles.
screen: M Vertica, Aster, Maxim 1050, Riana, EkoCheras, Shamelin Star, Green, Windows 2497 and Scot Pine retained as historical cases with the 7 October replay.
gaps: Original plans, actual operations and matched resales remain missing. Larger family, new-delivery and distressed expressions are uneven; no claim all Cheras projects screened.

name: South / southwest KL
finding: Citizen 2 is a compact affordability test, not a proxy for the family markets of Taman Desa, OUG or Bukit Jalil. Evidence disproves using its inconsistent lowest header as entry. At a clean advertised RM430k, rent/fee sensitivity can change standard coverage sign.
segments: RM430k/725-sqft 2BR worked. Family budget bands and premium products not bounded.
screen: Regional transaction scan surfaced 288 Residences, Residence 8, Seringin and Legacy OUG as follow-up candidates; transaction medians are not valuations.
gaps: Kuchai, Happy Garden/OUG, Taman Desa, Sri Petaling, Bukit Jalil and Sungai Besi/Chan Sow Lin lack new gate cases. Need family/compact contrast and supply at actual buyer budgets.

name: Petaling Jaya
finding: Pacific Place tests whether low-quantum access can survive furnishing, lease and mixed-use product issues. It cannot establish PJ-wide value or displace mature family products without a buyer-budget comparison.
segments: RM370k/864-sqft 2BR worked; premium family and larger mature stock absent.
screen: Regional source leads: Five Stones, Kelana Mahkota and Ken Damansara. Prior user observation about relative Sterling/Kelana Mahkota age remains a lead, not a current management judgment.
gaps: Old/New Town, established sections, SS2/Sea Park/Paramount, Kelana, Tropicana and Kota Damansara/Surian not worked here. Prior age/quality assumptions cannot rank them.

name: West / northwest premium and mature KL
finding: First Residence and OOAK deliberately contrast ordinary family quantum with premium one-bedroom rent. The former has furnishing/works/parking exposure; the latter cannot borrow large-family school demand. They are opportunity-cost alternatives, not direct valuation comparables.
screen: Mont Kiara/Arcoris and Kepong transaction scans were scope-filtered; no yield or appreciation from automated project summaries accepted.
gaps: TTDI, Bangsar South/Pantai/Kerinchi, Damansara Heights, Hartamas, Dutamas/Segambut, Desa ParkCity/Menjalara and Damansara Perdana/Mutiara remain without fresh cases. Their potential quality premium remains untested.

name: Central / east KL
finding: Angkasa Impian 2 tests a mature ordinary-tenancy expression in a central address. An incentive-heavy compact ask and old sparse transfers demonstrate why central location cannot substitute for effective consideration and current building evidence.
segments: RM440k/660-sqft 1BR worked; larger-family, new luxury and ordinary Ampang budgets unbounded.
screen: 28 Boulevard and Ampang Boulevard surfaced in regional scans. Angkasa larger 1100–1500-sqft sale/rent stock was examined diagnostically; old auction expression kept separate.
gaps: KLCC/Ampang Park, TRX, Tun Razak/Titiwangsa/Sentul, Jalan Ampang/Jelatek/Dato Keramat, Ampang Hilir and broader Ampang/Pandan not worked as full cases. No city-centre rent or owner-depth ranking.

name: Northeast / north
finding: PV21's attractive conditional arithmetic is held at price-identity resolution because the sale page calls the unit a rental. Wangsa Metroview is a contrasting mature-family lead, not a completed alternate case. Institutional proximity does not prove absorbed demand.
segments: RM310k/900-sqft marketed 2BR diagnostic only; consideration unresolved.
screen: Wangsa Metroview 1150-sqft sale/rent leads screened; shop-office yield and townhouse records excluded from high-rise residential comparison.
gaps: Gombak, Melawati/Ukay, Batu Caves/Selayang and Sungai Buloh/Kwasa lack fresh gate cases. Need original-family and newer-stock countercases before a northeast/north ranking.

name: Southwest / west Selangor
finding: Skypod supplies a concrete cross-region challenger to Cheras compact stock, while the official retail/office evidence prevents a false residential discount. Puchong's case does not cover the dispersed employment/housing markets westward.
segments: RM380k/881-sqft 2BR worked; RM410k alternative is diagnostic, not a second case.
screen: Skypod 1033/1248-sqft expressions and a Puchong condominium transaction index were screened; commercial offers excluded from investable scope.
gaps: Puchong Prima/South, Seri Kembangan/Serdang/Equine, Subang/USJ/Sunway, Subang Bestari, Shah Alam/Glenmarie, Setia Alam/Bukit Raja and Klang/Botanic/Bukit Tinggi remain without fresh full cases.

name: Outer growth corridors
finding: Solstice deliberately challenges a family-owner preference with an income-led small unit. University primary evidence supports a rental channel and also documents substitutes. This says nothing yet about high-rise adoption in landed-led outer townships.
segments: RM200k/450-sqft 1BR marketed expression worked; residential rights/plan unresolved. Family and new-launch budgets unbounded.
screen: Solstice larger layouts and Cyberjaya accommodation alternatives examined; commercial Cybersquare records and name collisions excluded from adopted residential value.
gaps: Kajang/Bangi, Semenyih, Putrajaya, Dengkil/Kota Warisan/Salak Tinggi, Kota Kemuning/Rimbayu/Tropicana Aman/Eco Sanctuary, Elmina and Rawang/Gamuda Gardens/Kundang require dedicated buyer/supply cases.
